message.abstract: <jats:p>Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) becomes challenging when trustworthy visible information and locally degraded responses coexist within a single image. Texture and scene appearance may remain useful in some regions, whereas other regions exhibit low-light darkness, low contrast, glare-like washout, or saturation/overexposure and therefore require selective treatment during fusion. Existing approaches to degraded IVIF inputs improve robustness, but do not fully explore how local trustworthiness should coordinaterepresentation learning, information transfer, and supervision. To address this gap, we propose RePrior, a framework based on reliability-anchored factorized priors. Weak regional cues anchor reliable and unreliable components with a two-component Gaussian mixture prior over source-specific visible features. Simultaneously, joint factorized-prior matching regularizes the organization of modality-common and source-specific representations. The resulting soft unreliable-component assignment drives two distinct controls: a strict gate for visible-detail transfer and a more tolerant gate for appearance preservation. This design suppresses degradation-dominated responses without uniformly discarding valid smooth regions. Across four IVIF benchmarks, RePrior ranks among the top two in 15 of 16 dataset--metric comparisons against 11 representative methods. Mechanism-oriented ablations support the intended prior semantics,shared/private latent organization, and role-specific control, whiledownstream perception evaluations further support practical utility. Inseparately trained secondary studies, the same reliability-conditionedscaffold is adapted to multi-exposure fusion (MEF), multi-focus fusion (MFF),and medical image fusion (MIF) by defining reliability as local exposureusefulness, focus/sharpness confidence, and local information confidence,respectively, yielding top-two results on four of five metrics in each task.</jats:p>
title: RePrior: Reliability-Anchored Factorized Priors for Infrared--Visible Image Fusion under Local Visible-Image Degradation
